notes.meaning: Jesus finished preaching His sermon openly to the crowd and entered Capernaum, the town where He lived during His public ministry. His spoken words were now followed by mighty miracles that proved His power and authority. He showed that the truth He taught was backed up by divine power.

A Roman military officer called a centurion had a servant who was near death from illness. The officer valued this servant highly and cared deeply for his well-being. While many masters in that day were harsh to their servants, this officer treated his with genuine kindness and respect.

When the centurion heard that Jesus was near, he asked respected Jewish leaders to plead for his dying servant. Because he was a Gentile—someone who was not Jewish—he felt unworthy to approach Jesus directly. He showed both deep love for his servant and great respect for the Lord.

The Jewish leaders came to Jesus and begged Him earnestly to help the officer. They argued that he deserved this favor because he loved their nation and had even paid to build their synagogue, or house of worship. While the leaders judged him by his good works, the centurion came to Jesus with a humble heart.

Jesus started walking with the leaders toward the officer's house. Before He arrived, the centurion sent friends to ask Him not to go to any trouble, saying he was not worthy to have Jesus enter his home. The officer recognized his own unworthiness in the presence of the Lord.

The centurion explained that his feeling of unworthiness was why he did not meet Jesus in person. He asked Jesus simply to speak a word, knowing that would be enough to heal the servant. He trusted that Christ did not need to be physically present to heal.

As an army officer, the centurion understood how command worked. He knew that when he gave an order, his soldiers obeyed right away. He saw that Jesus had supreme authority over sickness, so that any disease would instantly obey His command.

Jesus was amazed when He heard the centurion's humble and confident words. He turned to the crowd following Him and said He had not found such great faith anywhere in Israel. This Roman soldier showed a strong trust that even God's covenant people had failed to display.

When the messengers returned to the centurion's house, they found the servant completely healthy. Jesus healed him from a distance without ever stepping foot inside the home. This showed that Christ's power to heal knows no limits of space or time.

The next day, Jesus traveled to a small town named Nain, accompanied by His disciples and a large crowd. Walking with many people meant there would be many witnesses to what happened next. Jesus continued His daily work of doing good wherever He went.

Near the town gate, Jesus met a funeral crowd carrying out a dead young man for burial outside the city walls. He was the only son of his mother, and she was already a widow with no husband to protect her. A large group from the town walked beside her to share in her deep grief.

When the Lord saw the weeping mother, His heart was moved with deep pity for her. No one asked Him for help, but He stepped forward out of pure kindness and told her to stop crying. He had the power to take away her sorrow because He was about to give her son back.

Jesus stepped up and touched the open wooden frame carrying the body, and the bearers stopped moving. Touching a dead body usually made a person ceremonially unclean, but Jesus brought life instead. Then He spoke with divine authority, commanding the young man to get up.

The dead man sat up immediately and began to speak, giving clear proof that he was alive again. Jesus gently handed the living son back to his rejoicing mother. In this miracle of mercy, Jesus showed His absolute victory over death.

A deep sense of awe and holy fear came over all the people, and they gave praise to God. They declared that a great prophet—a messenger speaking for God—had arrived among them and that God had visited His people with mercy. They recognized that God was actively moving to help them once again.

The report of this astonishing resurrection spread quickly through all of Judea and the regions around it. People everywhere heard that Jesus had raised a dead man back to life. This exciting news soon reached John the Baptist in his prison cell.

John's disciples visited him in prison and told him about all the wonders Jesus was doing. Even though John was locked away by King Herod, God's work was moving forward powerfully through Jesus. The news gave John's followers plenty to think about.

John called two of his disciples and sent them to ask Jesus if He was the promised Messiah or if they should wait for someone else. The Messiah was the Savior and King promised throughout the Old Testament. This question gave Jesus the opportunity to show clearly who He was.

differ.view: John did not doubt for himself, but sent his disciples so their doubts would be settled by seeing Jesus firsthand.
John himself was wrestling with doubt in prison because Jesus was not bringing the swift political deliverance he had expected.

notes.meaning: The two messengers arrived and repeated John's exact question to Jesus. They asked whether He was the promised Savior or if they should continue looking for another leader. They wanted a direct answer from the Lord Himself.

Right at that moment, Jesus healed many people of painful diseases, freed those oppressed by evil spirits, and gave sight to the blind. Instead of simply answering with words, He let John's disciples watch His miracles with their own eyes. His actions demonstrated His power and divine calling.

Jesus told the messengers to go back and tell John what they had witnessed. The blind could see, the lame could walk, lepers were made clean, the deaf could hear, the dead were raised, and the poor heard the good news. These works matched the ancient promises in the Scriptures about what the true Messiah would do.

Jesus added that anyone who does not lose faith or take offense at Him is truly blessed. Many people expected the Messiah to be an earthly ruler who would overthrow Rome, and they were disappointed by His humble ministry. True happiness comes to those who trust Jesus without stumbling over how He works.

Once John's messengers left, Jesus began speaking to the crowds about John so His praise would not sound like flattery. He asked them what they went into the desert to see, asking if John was like a tall grass reed that bends with every gust of wind. Jesus made it clear that John was not fickle, but stood firm for the truth like a rock.

Jesus asked if they had gone out to see a man dressed in fancy, soft clothing. People who wear fine robes and enjoy easy living belong in royal palaces, not in the rugged wilderness. John lived a simple, disciplined life so he could faithfully point people back to God.
